steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Three inter-related forces that set the stage for the outbreak of World War I were:

1. Militarism and the arms race  
   • In the decades before 1914, Europe’s great powers poured money and prestige into ever-larger armies and navies, embraced detailed war plans such as Germany’s Schlieffen Plan, and glorified military values at home.  The belief that decisive war was both feasible and even desirable made political crises far more likely to escalate into open conflict.

2. The rigid system of entangling alliances  
   • Two heavily armed blocs—Germany and Austria-Hungary (later joined by the Ottoman Empire) versus France, Russia, and, eventually, Britain—had pledged mutual defense.  What might have remained a limited Balkan clash in the summer of 1914 instead drew in every major European power within days as treaty obligations activated like falling dominoes.

3. Nationalism (including imperial and ethnic rivalries)  
   • Fierce national pride intensified competition for colonies and influence (for example, in Africa and the Balkans) and fueled separatist movements within multi-ethnic empires such as Austria-Hungary.  Serbian nationalism inspired Gavrilo Princip’s assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914—the immediate spark that ignited the pre-existing powder keg.
